terms.gloss: it is right, it is allowed (to)
terms.grammar: indeclinable noun with est; the person in the dative: fās tibi est, you have the right
evidence: Ov. Met. 4.428: fās est et ab hoste docērī
Traupman 107: you have every right to …, omne fās tibi est (+ inf.)
terms.comment: Fās is what divine and natural law allow, so it is right and proper; its opposite is nefās. Traupman’s omne fās tibi est, “every right is yours”, strengthens it; the phrase itself is not quoted in Lewis & Short.

phrases.latin: fās est et ab hoste docērī
phrases.english: it is right to learn even from an enemy
